records.title: 1.5L Turbo Charge Air Cooler (Intercooler) Condensation Restricting Airflow — Underboost / Reduced Engine Power
records.description: On 1.5L turbo (LYX) Equinox models, moisture accumulates inside the charge air cooler (intercooler) and, in cold or highly humid weather, can freeze or pool enough to severely restrict intake airflow. This trips turbo underboost/MAP faults and pushes the engine into 'Engine Power Reduced' limp mode with sluggish acceleration. A related GM TSB also documents the charge air cooler outlet tube separating from the throttle body on 2018-2022 1.5L turbo models, producing the same reduced-power symptom. This is distinct from the known coolant-loss/intercooler-condensation head-gasket issue — here the failure is airflow restriction and boost loss, not coolant consumption.
records.solution: Inspect and reseat or replace the charge air cooler outlet duct/clamp at the throttle body per GM TSB; clear accumulated condensate from the intercooler; verify the CAC and ducting for cracks. Reprogram the ECM if a related calibration update applies. Some owners drill a small factory-spec weep provision or follow the TSB ducting repair.
symptoms: Engine Power Reduced warning / limp mode
Loss of acceleration and turbo boost
Worse in cold or humid weather

records.title: 1.5L turbo coolant loss / overheating (head gasket & intercooler condensation)
records.description: The 1.5L turbo (LYX) in 2018+ Equinox is reported to lose coolant with no obvious external leak, leading to overheating and, in some cases, head-gasket failure (coolant entering the combustion chamber). Owners describe the coolant level dropping over time with overheating events. Separately, the early 1.5L turbo had an intercooler/charge-pipe condensation problem in very cold climates where moisture freezes and blocks airflow, triggering reduced-power conditions; GM updated the intercooler and charge-pipe design on later builds.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system and perform a combustion-gas (block) test to confirm head-gasket involvement when coolant disappears without an external leak. Repair/replace the head gasket as needed and inspect for warpage. For cold-climate condensation/limp-mode complaints, install the updated intercooler and charge-pipe parts. Monitor coolant level and address overheating immediately to avoid further engine damage.
symptoms: Coolant level drops with no visible leak
White exhaust smoke or sweet smell
Reduced engine power / limp mode in cold weather
Coolant in oil or low coolant warnings

records.title: 1.5L Turbo Fuel Injector Leak Causing Misfire, Fuel Odor and Rough Running
records.description: The direct-injection fuel injectors on the 1.5L turbo can leak - internally past a cracked injector body/tip (dumping raw fuel into the cylinder and causing a misfire) or externally past worn upper O-rings (fuel smell, weeping at the rail). This is distinct from the covered high-pressure fuel-pump and in-tank fuel-pump-module failures. GM issued a Customer Satisfaction Program for a fuel-injector leak on some 2025 Equinox that directs dealers to replace all four injectors and the fuel feed pipe.
records.solution: Diagnose with fuel trims, a misfire counter, and a visual/smell check at the fuel rail. Replace the leaking injector - GM guidance for the 2025 program replaces all four injectors, the rail bolts, and the fuel feed intermediate pipe. For O-ring-only external leaks, new upper O-rings may suffice. Check for any open Customer Satisfaction Program by VIN. Repairs commonly $750-$1,000.

records.title: 1.5L Turbo Intake Valve Carbon Buildup Causing Misfires and Rough Cold Start (GDI)
records.description: Because the 1.5L turbo (and the earlier 2.4L SIDI) is a gasoline direct-injection engine, no fuel washes over the back of the intake valves. Over 40k-80k miles, oil vapor from the PCV system bakes onto the valves as hard carbon, restricting airflow and disrupting the seal. Owners report a check-engine light with single- or multi-cylinder misfires that are worst on a cold start, plus a slight loss of power and rougher idle. GM technical document PIP5029E acknowledges misfires caused by 'major carbon build up on the intake and/or exhaust valves.'
records.solution: Confirm with fuel trims and a borescope of the intake valves. The definitive fix is walnut-shell media blasting of the intake ports to physically remove the deposits (typically $300-$600). Top-tier fuel and periodic intake/induction cleaners (e.g., CRC GDI IVD, GM Top Engine Cleaner) slow accumulation but will not fully clear heavy deposits. Address any leaking PCV/oil-separator that is feeding oil vapor into the intake, and keep to shorter oil-change intervals to reduce future buildup.
symptoms: Check engine light with misfire codes
Rough or shaky idle, worst on cold start
Slight loss of power and fuel economy
Occasional stumble that may not always be felt by the driver

records.title: 1.6L Diesel NOx Sensor Failure / DEF System Faults Causing Reduced Power and Limp Mode
records.description: The diesel Equinox (1.6L LH7) is prone to NOx-sensor and diesel-exhaust-fluid (DEF/SCR) emissions faults. Failing or out-of-calibration NOx sensors and reductant-injection problems set codes such as P11DB (NOx sensor 1 performance) and P249D (closed-loop reductant control at limit), trigger a 'service emissions system' warning with a countdown, and ultimately force the vehicle into a speed-limited limp mode to protect the SCR catalyst. Owners report repeat failures because GM revised the NOx sensors multiple times. A holed/leaking charge-air cooler can also let unmetered air in and mimic the same emissions faults, so the intake must be checked too. This is a high-stakes, expensive emissions issue for the relatively rare but enthusiast-tracked diesel.
records.solution: Scan and record all emissions DTCs (e.g., P11DB, P249D) and freeze-frame data. Verify DEF quality and the DEF/reductant injector and pump operation, then test the upstream/downstream NOx sensors against live SCR data. Replace the failed NOx sensor with the latest revised GM part for this engine (verify the exact PN by VIN, as GM issued multiple revisions — a wrong NOx sensor will not resolve the fault). Inspect the charge-air cooler and intake for leaks/holes that can trigger the same limp mode. After repair, perform the required relearn/forced regeneration and confirm the countdown/limp-mode clears.
symptoms: 'Service emissions system' / DEF warning with mileage or speed-limit countdown
Reduced engine power and limp mode at low speed
Check-engine light with NOx/SCR codes (P11DB, P249D)

records.title: 2.4L Ecotec excessive oil consumption (worn/stuck oil-control piston rings)
records.description: The 2.4L Ecotec (LAF/LEA) four-cylinder used in 2010-2017 Equinox (and its GMC Terrain twin) consumes oil at an abnormal rate — frequently as much as 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles — due to low-tension/stuck oil-control piston rings combined with PCV-system issues that draw oil past the rings. Owners report blue exhaust smoke on startup and acceleration, low-oil warnings between changes, and in severe cases engine damage when the oil level drops unnoticed. GM acknowledged the defect in a 2015 service bulletin instructing dealers to replace the four piston assemblies on affected engines, and nearly 400 NHTSA complaints describe the same failure. A $42M class-action settlement (final approval Nov 2019) covered 2010-2013 vehicles, and a January 2023 suit extended claims to 2014-2017 units.
records.solution: Have an oil-consumption test performed (documented quart-per-mile measurement) to qualify for goodwill/settlement coverage. The proper repair is replacement of all four piston assemblies with updated rings; clean or replace the PCV orifice and check for carbon buildup. Check oil at every fuel fill as an interim measure to avoid running low. If out of coverage, expect ring/piston replacement or, where the engine was damaged from oil starvation, a long-block replacement.
symptoms: Low oil level between changes / oil light comes on
Blue smoke from exhaust on startup or acceleration
Burning more than 1 quart per 1,000-2,000 miles
Engine knock or damage if run low on oil

records.title: 2.4L Ecotec timing/balance chain stretch from tensioner & low oil
records.description: The 2.4L Ecotec in 2010-2017 Equinox is prone to premature timing-chain and balance-chain stretch, driven primarily by a collapsing chain tensioner and made worse by the engine's known oil-consumption problem (low oil reduces hydraulic pressure to the tensioner). Symptoms are a rattle at cold startup, a check-engine light, and rough running or loss of power. Because the engine is an interference design, a chain that skips timing far enough lets the valves contact the pistons, turning a maintenance item into an engine-destroying failure. GM issued Special Coverage Adjustment 12313D covering premature timing/balance chain wear on certain 2010-2011 2.4L engines.
records.solution: Diagnose with cam/crank correlation codes and inspect chain stretch. Replace the full timing chain kit (chains, guides, tensioners) and the balance chain; correct any underlying oil consumption first or the new chain will wear early. Address promptly at first rattle — driving on a stretched chain risks valve-to-piston contact and a totaled engine.
symptoms: Check engine light with cam-crank correlation codes

records.title: 2.4L Exhaust Manifold Cracking Causing Exhaust Leak and Cabin Fumes
records.description: The integrated exhaust manifold on the 2.4L Ecotec is prone to cracking, producing a loud ticking/exhaust-leak sound that is loudest on a cold start and can fade as the metal expands. Beyond the noise, the leak can allow exhaust fumes into the cabin and set oxygen-sensor/misfire-adjacent codes. The problem is often aggravated by the 2.4L's well-known oil consumption (a clogged converter raises backpressure) and repeat failures within a couple of years are commonly reported.
records.solution: Inspect the manifold cold for cracks and check for a leaking manifold-to-pipe gasket and broken/rusted studs. Replace the cracked manifold (or the integrated manifold/converter assembly on federal-emissions cars) with new gaskets and studs. Address underlying oil consumption to protect the new converter. Repairs typically $400-$900 depending on whether the catalytic section is integrated.

records.title: 3.0L / 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Stretch Causing Rattle and P0008/P0016 Codes
records.description: GM's high-feature V6 in the Equinox suffers premature timing-chain stretch, distinct from the covered 2.4L chain issue. The classic symptom is a rattle or chain-slap on cold start from the front/passenger side of the engine. Long oil-change intervals and low oil accelerate the wear; left unfixed, a chain can jump time or break and bend valves.
records.solution: Verify with the correlation codes and a cam-timing check; do not keep driving with active correlation codes. Replace the timing chains, guides, and tensioners as a complete updated kit (both banks on the V6), and change oil on time with the correct spec afterward. This is a labor-intensive repair, commonly $2,000-$3,500.

records.title: 6T70/6T75 transmission shudder, hard shifts & 3-5-reverse wave plate failure
records.description: Equinox models with the GM 6T70/6T75 six-speed automatic suffer shudder, harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, and loss of reverse. A common root cause is failure of the 3-5-reverse wave plate, which can crack and cause extreme shudder when reverse is engaged and eventual loss of drive. Overheated/degraded fluid that loses viscosity accelerates internal wear. Failures typically appear between roughly 60,000 and 150,000 miles. Owners report bucking when engaging gear, failure to shift out of 2nd, and inability to engage reverse.
records.solution: Service the fluid on a strict interval (and after any overheating). For wave-plate failure, the transmission must be removed and rebuilt with the updated/stronger wave plate; a fluid-and-filter service alone will not fix a cracked wave plate. Verify a current 6T70 software/calibration update is installed to address shudder/shift quality.
symptoms: Slipping or failure to move from a stop

records.description: A known safety issue on later first-generation Equinox models involves corrosion in the brake pressure modulator valve (BPMV), which can cause the ABS to activate improperly at low speeds. records.title: A/C Compressor Self-Destructs and Contaminates the Entire System With Metal Debris
records.description: A well-documented and expensive failure mode: the A/C compressor on the 2010-2017 Equinox platform fails internally and grenades, shedding fine aluminum/metal particles ("black death") that circulate through the entire refrigerant system. Owners notice the A/C suddenly stops blowing cold, sometimes with a grinding/clunking noise or a seized clutch. Because the debris contaminates the condenser, lines, orifice/expansion device, and accumulator, simply bolting on a new compressor causes the replacement to fail almost immediately. A proper repair requires replacing the compressor AND condenser/accumulator and thoroughly flushing the system. This drives repair bills well above a simple compressor swap and is a top owner complaint on these years.
records.solution: When the compressor has failed internally, do not just replace it. Replace the A/C compressor and the condenser and accumulator/receiver-drier, replace the orifice tube/expansion valve, and flush all serviceable lines and the evaporator until clean of metal debris. Pull a proper vacuum, recharge to spec, and add the correct PAG oil charge. Compressor part numbers vary by year/engine on this platform (e.g., ACDelco 15-22343 and 15-22276 for 2010-2011, 15-22330 for 2015-2017), so verify the exact PN by VIN before ordering. Skipping the flush/condenser is the most common reason a replacement compressor fails again quickly.
symptoms: A/C suddenly blows warm and never cools again
Grinding, clunking, or rattling from the compressor; seized or chattering clutch
Metal/aluminum debris found in the refrigerant or accumulator
Replacement compressor fails shortly after install (system not flushed)

records.title: A/C condenser refrigerant leak (warm air from vents)
records.description: The air-conditioning condenser on the Equinox commonly develops refrigerant leaks at its tubes and seals, or from stone-chip damage to the front-mounted core. Because the condenser's internal tubes and seals cannot be serviced individually, a leak requires full condenser replacement. The classic symptom is the A/C blowing warm air, often with an oily, grimy residue visible on the condenser where refrigerant and PAG oil have escaped. This is a frequently reported wear item across multiple model years, especially 2016-2017.
records.solution: Perform a dye/electronic leak test to confirm the condenser is the source. Replace the A/C condenser, evacuate and recharge the system to spec, and replace the receiver/drier or desiccant as recommended. Inspect for stone-chip damage and consider a condenser guard in high-debris environments.

records.title: Catalytic Converter Failure (P0420) Caused by Oil-Burning — GM Special Coverage 15810
records.description: On the 2.4L Ecotec Equinox, the catalytic converter is frequently destroyed by the engine's chronic oil consumption (worn piston rings) — burned oil coats and thermally damages the catalyst, setting P0420 (catalyst efficiency below threshold) and the check-engine light. Replacing only the converter without first fixing the oil-consumption root cause leads to rapid re-failure of the new cat. GM acknowledged the thermal/erosion converter failures with Special Coverage 15810, extending coverage to 10 years / 120,000 miles on affected 2010-2011 LAF-engine vehicles. This is a high-demand search because owners face an expensive converter plus the underlying ring/oil repair, and aftermarket "universal" cats often won't clear the code.
records.solution: Diagnose P0420 properly (verify upstream/downstream O2 behavior; rule out exhaust leaks and bad O2 sensors). Critically, fix the oil-consumption root cause first — perform the GM oil-consumption repair (piston rings, per the applicable GM oil-consumption PI/TSB) or the new converter will fail again. Replace with a quality OE-grade catalytic converter (cheap universal cats often won't keep P0420 from returning). Check eligibility for GM Special Coverage 15810 (10 yr / 120k mi) on 2010-2011 LAF vehicles for converter replacement. Clear codes and run a drive cycle to confirm the catalyst monitor passes.
symptoms: Check-engine light with code P0420 (catalyst efficiency below threshold)
Elevated oil consumption preceding the converter failure
Reduced fuel economy and sluggish performance
Repeat P0420 after a cheap aftermarket cat was installed

records.title: Coolant Surge Tank / Reservoir Cracking Causing Slow Coolant Loss
records.description: The plastic coolant surge/recovery tank on second-generation (2010-2017) Equinox becomes brittle from years of heat and pressure cycling and develops hairline cracks, most often at the seams or around the cap neck. This causes a slow, mysterious coolant loss with occasional sweet smell and pink/orange residue near the front of the engine, and if ignored can progress to overheating. This is distinct from the 1.5T head-gasket coolant loss and the 3.4L V6 head-gasket leak.
records.solution: Pressure-test the cooling system to confirm the tank (not a hose, water pump, or radiator) is the source. Replace the surge tank and its cap with a new assembly; plastic-weld repairs rarely hold under pressure. Refill with the correct DEX-COOL and bleed the system. Parts are inexpensive (aftermarket tanks ~$30-$80, GM assembly more); total job typically $150-$400.
symptoms: Gradually dropping coolant level with no obvious puddle
Dried pink/orange residue on or below the reservoir
Visible crack or seepage at the tank seam or cap

records.title: Engine-driven brake vacuum pump failure causing sudden hard brake pedal
records.description: Third-generation Equinox (2018-2022) uses a camshaft-driven mechanical vacuum pump mounted at the rear of the cylinder head to supply the brake booster (the turbo intake is pressurized, so there is no manifold vacuum). This pump can seize and its drive gear break, suddenly eliminating brake assist — the pedal becomes 'hard as a rock' with greatly increased stopping distances. In severe cases the pump shatters and sends metal debris into the engine, causing catastrophic internal damage. NHTSA has over 300 complaints; a related GM recall (19V645000) reprogrammed the brake control module on other models but excluded the Equinox/Terrain, and a February 2026 class action (Thieme v. General Motors) targets 2018-2022 Equinox/Terrain.
records.solution: If the brake pedal suddenly goes hard, stop driving and tow the vehicle — continued driving risks a crash and possible engine destruction. Replace the failed vacuum pump (and brake booster if damaged); inspect for metal debris in the engine if the pump came apart. Check VIN for any applicable recall/special coverage and document the complaint with NHTSA.
symptoms: Greatly increased stopping distance / loss of power assist
Noise from rear of engine before failure

records.title: EVAP Canister Purge Valve Stuck Open Causing P0496 / Rough Running (3.0L & 3.6L V6)
records.description: The vapor-canister purge solenoid on the V6 Equinox (and Terrain) commonly fails stuck-open, letting fuel vapor flow into the intake when it shouldn't. This sets DTC P0496 (EVAP flow during a non-purge condition) and sometimes P0455/P0446, illuminates the check-engine light, and can cause a rough/rich idle, hard starting, and even a faint fuel smell. It is one of the most frequently replaced emissions parts on the V6 Equinox because the valve is a known weak point and the repair is cheap and easy. The valve sits on top of the engine and is a roughly one-hour DIY job.
records.solution: Confirm P0496 and inspect the purge-valve vacuum lines for cracks and the connector for damage before replacing. Replace the vapor canister purge valve with the GM/ACDelco OE part 12690512 (supersedes 12610560). After replacement, clear codes and run a drive cycle to confirm the EVAP monitor passes and the light stays off. Also verify the gas cap and EVAP lines if leak codes (P0455/P0446) accompany the purge code.
symptoms: Check-engine light with code P0496 (sometimes P0455/P0446)
Rough or rich idle, occasional stumble
Hard starting, especially right after refueling

records.title: Front Wheel Bearing and Hub Assembly Failure Triggering ABS/Traction Warnings
records.description: Premature front wheel bearing and hub assembly wear is a common issue on the 2005-2009 Equinox. records.solution: Diagnosis involves road-testing for bearing noise, checking for wheel play, and scanning ABS data for an intermittent or weak wheel speed signal. records.title: Head Gasket Coolant Leak and Overheating on 3.4L V6
records.description: The first-generation Equinox commonly uses the GM 3.4L LA1 V6, and owners have repeatedly reported coolant loss, overheating, and eventual head gasket failure. In many cases the problem starts as an external or internal coolant leak, then progresses to overheating, rough running, white exhaust smoke, or coolant contamination. This issue is well documented in owner complaints and repair discussions for the 2005-2009 Equinox/Torrent platform.
records.solution: Diagnosis usually includes pressure-testing the cooling system, checking for combustion gases in the coolant, inspecting for coolant loss with no visible leak, and verifying whether the engine has been overheated. Repair typically involves replacing the head gaskets, checking head flatness, resurfacing if needed, and replacing related components such as intake gaskets, head bolts, thermostat, and coolant. If overheating was severe, the cylinder heads or engine may also need machine work or replacement.

records.title: Heater Core and HVAC Case Water Leak Causing Wet Passenger Floor
records.description: A recurring complaint on first-generation Equinox models is water or coolant intrusion into the passenger-side floor area. Owners report either a leaking heater core/coolant smell inside the cabin or water entering through HVAC case drains and cowl sealing issues, leaving carpets soaked and windows fogged. The problem can lead to mold, electrical connector corrosion under the carpet, and persistent interior odor.
records.solution: The source needs to be identified first: coolant residue and sweet odor point toward the heater core, while clear water after rain or A/C use suggests a blocked evaporator drain or body sealing issue. Repairs may include heater core replacement, clearing the A/C drain, resealing cowl/body seams, and drying the carpet and underlayment thoroughly to prevent mold and connector damage.

records.title: High-Pressure Direct-Injection Fuel Pump Failure Causing Stalling and Limp Mode (1.5L Turbo)
records.description: Owners of 2023-2024 Equinox models with the 1.5L turbo (LYX) report the engine-mounted high-pressure direct-injection fuel pump failing, often well under 60,000 miles (some as early as 28,000 miles). The pump can no longer maintain rail pressure, so the engine suddenly loses power, drops into 'Engine Power Reduced' limp mode (speed limited to roughly 5-55 mph), stalls, or won't restart, frequently leaving the vehicle undrivable and requiring a tow. CarComplaints logged 20 distinct 2023 fuel/propulsion complaints centered on this part, and many owners report the replacement pump being on national back-order for months. This is a separate failure from the earlier 2021-2022 in-tank low-pressure fuel pump module recall.
records.solution: Dealer diagnoses low fuel-rail pressure and replaces the high-pressure fuel pump (and gaskets); some cases also require fuel injectors or rail cleaning. Out of warranty, repairs have run roughly $1,000-$1,100. Owners should check for any GM warranty extension or special coverage and verify it is the high-pressure pump (not the in-tank module) before paying out of pocket.

records.title: Inaccurate Fuel Gauge / Fuel-Level Sender Misreading (Tank Reads Wrong, Won't Reach Full)
records.description: A very common 2018+ Equinox complaint: the fuel gauge is wildly inaccurate. Owners report the needle never reaches Full even after topping off (often reading ~3/4), drops or jumps erratically, or hits 'E' with many gallons still in the tank — making it nearly impossible to judge real range. The cause is a fuel-level sender/fuel-pump module that does not seat correctly in the bottom of the tank (insulator pads interfere with sender float travel) and/or sender wiring/ground faults. Dealers have told customers the issue affects essentially all 2018 Equinox/Terrain units, and swapping clusters or senders alone often does not fix it without correcting the module seating.
records.solution: Diagnose by graphing fuel-level sender voltage vs. actual fuel added; confirm whether the gauge tracks linearly. The documented correction is to drop the tank, remove the interfering insulator pads from the bottom of the fuel-pump/sender module, and verify the sender float travels its full range and seats correctly. Inspect the sender connector and grounds for corrosion. If the sender card itself is worn, replace the fuel-level sender / fuel-pump module assembly (verify exact PN by VIN). Re-calibrate/relearn if required and road-test from full to confirm accurate readings.
symptoms: Gauge never reads Full even after the tank is topped off
Needle reads Empty with several gallons still remaining
Reading jumps or drops erratically while driving
Problem persists after a cluster swap

records.title: Infotainment / MyLink Display Goes Black or Reboots Repeatedly
records.description: The center touchscreen (Chevrolet MyLink / Infotainment 3) intermittently goes completely black, freezes, or reboots in a loop while the rest of the car operates normally. Owners lose the backup camera, climate display, radio, Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, and OnStar screen. The failure is usually a software/HMI-module fault but is also commonly traced to loose or corroded connectors and cables at the radio receiver located behind/below the glove box, or to a failing HMI (Human-Machine Interface) display module. A temporary fix is a system reboot (hold the power/volume knob ~10-15 s, or hold Home + fast-forward for 10 s), but it returns until the underlying module or wiring is addressed. This is one of the most-searched Equinox electrical complaints across model years.
records.solution: First attempt the documented soft reset (press and hold the power/volume knob 10-15 seconds, or Home + Seek-Forward for 10 seconds) and let the system reboot. If blackouts persist, inspect and reseat the connectors/cables at the radio receiver behind/below the glove box and check for corrosion or a poor ground. Apply any available GM infotainment software update at the dealer. If the HMI display module itself is failing, replace it with a GM-programmed HMI module (plug-and-play replacements are available and are reflashed to the VIN). Confirm CarPlay/camera/climate all return after repair.

Screen reboots in a loop or freezes on the Chevrolet logo

records.title: P0430 — Bank 2 Catalytic Converter Efficiency Loss on V6 Equinox
records.description: P0430 flags the rear cylinder bank's catalytic converter as no longer scrubbing exhaust efficiently. Because Bank 2 only exists on the V6 Equinox (the 3.4L LNJ of 2005-2009 and the 3.0L LF1 / 3.6L LFW/LFX of 2010-2017), this code is effectively a V6-only complaint — inline-4 Equinox models have only Bank 1. On these transverse V6s, Bank 2 is the firewall (rear) bank, whose exhaust manifold and downstream (post-cat) oxygen sensor are the hardest to reach. The ECM compares the upstream and downstream O2 sensor waveforms; when the rear converter can no longer store oxygen, the downstream sensor begins to mirror the upstream sensor and the code sets. On the Equinox the two most common root causes are a lazy/aged downstream (Bank 2, sensor 2) oxygen sensor giving a false reading, and a genuinely degraded rear catalytic converter — the 3.6L in particular has a documented cat-substrate/flange failure pattern (GM TSB 17-NA-321), and its known oil consumption can accelerate substrate poisoning.
records.solution: Confirm no misfire or fuel-trim codes are present first (fix those before the cat, or a new converter will fail again). Compare Bank 2 upstream vs downstream O2 sensor data on a scan tool — a downstream sensor that switches rapidly with the upstream one indicates a worn converter; a flat/lazy downstream sensor points to the sensor itself. Replace the Bank 2 downstream O2 sensor first when readings are ambiguous (cheaper), and replace the rear catalytic converter if the substrate is confirmed spent. Inspect the rear exhaust manifold and gaskets for leaks, which can also trip P0430.
symptoms: Check engine light on (often the only symptom)
May fail a state emissions/smog test

records.title: P0442 — Small EVAP Leak from Gas Cap Seal, Purge/Vent Solenoid, or Rusted EVAP Line
records.description: P0442 sets when the ECM detects a small evaporative-system leak — roughly a 0.020–0.040 inch hole's worth of pressure loss. On the Equinox this code follows a clear hierarchy of culprits. The single most common cause across all years is a degraded gas-cap O-ring that no longer seals (or a cap not clicked tight after refueling). On the second-generation 2.4L (LEA/LAF) and V6 models, the next most frequent offenders are the EVAP purge solenoid and the canister vent solenoid, which stick or leak internally. A cause that is distinctly an Equinox/Terrain pattern — especially in salt-belt states — is the metal EVAP line running under the driver's-side frame rail rusting through, which no amount of solenoid or gas-cap replacement will fix.
records.solution: Start with the cheapest, most likely fix: inspect the gas-cap O-ring for cracking/dry-rot and re-tighten until it clicks several times; replace with an OEM ACDelco cap if the seal is degraded. If the cap is good, perform a smoke test — this is the key step that separates a leaking purge/vent solenoid from a rusted-through metal EVAP line under the vehicle. Replace the purge or vent solenoid only if the smoke test localizes the leak there; if the underbody EVAP line is rusted, replace the line rather than throwing solenoids at it. Clear the code and complete a drive cycle to confirm.
symptoms: Occasional faint fuel odor near the tank
Hard start immediately after refueling (when purge/vent related)
No performance change; passes as a 'small leak'

records.title: P0700 — Transmission Fault Flag from 6T40/6T45 TCC Solenoid (Companion P0741)
records.description: P0700 is not a standalone defect — it is the transmission control module's way of telling the engine computer to turn on the check-engine light because a more specific transmission code is stored. On the second-generation Equinox, which uses GM's 6T40/6T45 six-speed automatic behind the 2.4L four-cylinder (and the 6T70 behind the V6), P0700 most often appears alongside P0741, Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) solenoid stuck-off. The TCC solenoid is a well-documented weak point across the 6T40/6T45/6T70 family: aged, unchanged transmission fluid lets debris cause the solenoid to stick, so the converter clutch won't lock up properly. P0700 can also accompany shift-solenoid performance codes. Because P0700 itself is generic, the actual fault must be read from the TCM's companion code — treating P0700 in isolation leads to misdiagnosis.
records.solution: Scan the TCM (not just generic powertrain codes) to retrieve the companion code — most commonly P0741 on this platform, or a shift-solenoid code. For a TCC/shift-solenoid fault, drop the transmission pan, replace the affected solenoid (many shops replace the solenoid set while the valve body is out), and service the fluid and filter — fresh fluid alone sometimes frees a mildly sticking TCC solenoid. Verify TCC slip speed returns to near zero when commanded on. If harsh shifting or limp mode is present, address it promptly to avoid further clutch/converter wear.
symptoms: Shudder or slipping at highway speed (TCC not locking)
Stuck in one gear / limp mode
Reduced fuel economy from converter not locking up

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Drain Tube Clog/Disconnect Causing Water in Cabin and Spare-Tire Well
records.description: On Equinox models with the panoramic/power sunroof, the four sunroof drain tubes are prone to clogging with debris or shrinking and popping off the sunroof tray fittings. Instead of routing rainwater/wash water down the A- and C-pillars and out under the vehicle, the water backs up and dumps inside — soaking the headliner, A-pillar trim, front carpet/footwells, rear seat area, and pooling in the spare-tire well. Owners frequently first notice damp carpet, a musty smell, or fogged windows before finding the source. Left unaddressed, the standing water in the spare well can corrode body metal and damage under-floor electrical connectors and modules. This is a high-volume owner complaint distinct from the rear-liftgate leak.
records.solution: Locate and clear all four sunroof drains (front pair exit near the front fenders/cowl, rear pair route down the C-pillars). Owners clear them with low-pressure compressed air or weed-trimmer line and verify flow by pouring water into each corner of the sunroof tray. If a rear drain tube has shrunk and disconnected, peel back the headliner/trim and reseat or replace the tube and clamp. Dry the carpet and padding thoroughly (and treat the spare well for any rust) to prevent mold and corrosion of under-floor connectors. Re-test by flooding each drain corner with water and confirming it exits underneath.

Water pooled in the spare-tire well / cargo floor
Damp headliner or water dripping from the A-pillar or dome light area

records.title: Power Liftgate Motor / Latch Actuator / Control Module Failure
records.description: On power-liftgate-equipped Equinox, the hands-free/power tailgate frequently stops working - it won't open, opens but won't latch closed, partially opens then stops, or won't hold itself up. records.title: Premature and Uneven Tire Wear From Rear Suspension Alignment (Rear Toe/Camber)

records.title: Shift-to-Park False Warning From Failing Park-Position Microswitch in Shifter Assembly
records.description: A widespread, heavily-searched complaint: the driver information center displays "Shift to Park" even though the lever is already fully in Park, and the vehicle then refuses to lock, refuses to allow the key/fob to leave, or will not restart. The root cause is an internal park-position microswitch inside the transmission-control (shifter) assembly whose contacts/actuator arm wear out and stop sending the correct low-voltage signal to the Body Control Module. It is intermittent at first (often heat- or vibration-related) and progresses to a daily no-start/no-lock condition. GM addressed it through service bulletins (e.g. PIT5616 series) rather than a recall, and the official repair is replacement of the entire shifter assembly because the switch is not sold separately. The same defect affects the platform-mate GMC Terrain and many other 2014-2024 GM models, which is why owner forums are full of it.
records.solution: Confirm the fault by checking for the park-switch signal (a scan tool will show the BCM not seeing Park). The GM-approved fix is to replace the complete automatic-transmission shift-control (shifter) assembly (e.g. GM PN 13540931 on 2022+ Equinox; the microswitch is not serviced separately). Many DIYers instead disassemble the shifter and replace/clean the worn internal microswitch. Apply any BCM update per the applicable PIT bulletin. After replacement, verify the DIC clears and the vehicle locks and restarts normally. Budget ~1-1.5 hours labor plus the assembly; aftermarket complete shifter assemblies are far cheaper than dealer OEM.

records.title: Steering Intermediate Shaft Clunk / Knock When Turning
records.description: A clunk, knock, or notchy feel through the steering wheel - most noticeable at low speed, during parking-lot maneuvers, or over bumps - traces to a worn/dry steering intermediate shaft or its universal joints. records.title: Windshield wiper failure from corroded wiper-transmission ball joints
records.description: Water and road debris intrude into the windshield wiper module/transmission ball joints, causing corrosion and excessive wear that detaches the linkage and leaves one or both wipers inoperative — a serious safety issue in rain/snow. GM recalled ~367,800 model-year 2013 Equinox/Terrain SUVs under NHTSA recall 16V582000 (Aug 2016), and later recalled 2014-2015 vehicles under recall 22V165 (2022). After an NHTSA investigation found high failure rates on 2010-2012 and 2016-2017 units that were not recalled, GM created Special Coverage Adjustment N192266181 covering wiper-transmission failures for 15 years / 200,000 miles.
records.solution: Check your VIN against recalls 16V582000 (2013) and 22V165 (2014-2015) at nhtsa.gov; affected vehicles get the wiper module/transmission inspected and replaced free. For 2010-2012 and 2016-2017 models, request repair under Special Coverage N192266181. Out of coverage, replace the wiper transmission/linkage assembly.
symptoms: One or both wipers stop working
Clicking/grinding from cowl area when wipers run

records.title: 1.5T Turbo PCV Valve and Oil Leak Issues
records.description: The 1.5L turbocharged engine experiences oil leaks near the dipstick tube and PCV valve-related crankcase pressure issues. A faulty PCV valve causes excessive crankcase pressure, which can lift the dipstick tube seal and cause oil leaks.
records.solution: Replace PCV valve. Reseal dipstick tube. Replace turbo if seals have failed. Clean intake system if oil contaminated. Use shorter oil change intervals (4,500-5,000 miles).
symptoms: Oil visible on top of engine near dipstick
Check engine light with PCV-related codes

records.title: 2.4L Ecotec Timing Chain Premature Failure
records.description: The 2.4L Ecotec engine is prone to premature timing chain failure due to improperly hardened chains and faulty tensioners. A defective batch of timing chains that were not hardened properly causes the chains to stretch prematurely. When the timing chain fails or jumps teeth on the sprockets, it can cause catastrophic valve damage and complete engine failure.
records.solution: Replace timing chain, tensioners, and guides. Inspect and replace damaged valves if timing jumped. Complete engine replacement if severe damage occurred. Check for GM Special Coverage letter for warranty extension.
symptoms: Check engine light with timing-related codes
Engine rattle or rattling noise on startup
Complete engine stall or failure to start

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain and Electrical System Issues
records.description: Equinox models are prone to parasitic battery drain where electrical components continue drawing power when the vehicle is off. Common culprits include the OnStar module, radio/infotainment system, interior lights, and stuck relays.
records.solution: Perform parasitic draw test to identify culprit. Replace faulty OnStar module. Update infotainment software. Replace radio/infotainment module if drawing excessive current. Install battery maintainer if vehicle sits for extended periods.
symptoms: Infotainment screen going black while driving

records.title: Electronic Power Steering Assist Loss
records.description: The electronic power steering (EPS) system can fail intermittently or completely, resulting in sudden loss of power steering assist. This creates a dangerous driving condition requiring significant physical effort to steer.
records.solution: Check and replace power steering fuse. Inspect wiring and ground connections to EPS module. Replace EPS control module. Replace steering column motor assembly. Verify proper battery voltage and charging system.
symptoms: Dashboard warning lights accompanying steering issues

records.description: A defective oil filter adapter can cause engine oil leaks that may contact hot exhaust components, creating a fire risk. Combined with the excessive oil consumption issue, low oil conditions can exacerbate the problem.
records.solution: Replace oil filter adapter assembly. Inspect and clean exhaust components of oil residue. Check for recall eligibility and have repair performed. Address any other oil leaks concurrently.

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption (2.4L Piston Ring Defect)
records.description: The 2.4L Ecotec engine uses low-tension piston rings that fail to maintain proper tension to keep oil in the crankcase. Vehicles consume 1 quart of oil per 800-1,000 miles. This defect can cause premature engine wear, engine failure, and potential fire risk if oil levels drop critically low. GM acknowledged this defect through TSBs and class action settlements.
records.solution: Piston ring replacement (may not be permanent fix). Complete piston assembly replacement with updated GM parts. Engine replacement with revised long block. Check eligibility for Special Coverage Adjustment 16118.
symptoms: Need to add oil frequently between changes
Engine knocking when oil is low

records.title: Fuel Pump Module Failure Causing Engine Stall
records.description: The fuel pump module fails to consistently provide adequate fuel flow to the engine, causing potential stalling while driving. This creates a significant safety hazard as the engine can stall unexpectedly in traffic. GM issued recall N222372310 affecting 23,164 vehicles.
records.solution: Fuel pump module replacement under recall N222372310. Contact dealer for recall service. Check VIN at my.gm.com/recalls for eligibility.

records.title: Transmission Shudder and Torque Converter Failure
records.description: Transmission shuddering is common in Equinox models, typically caused by torque converter clutch issues or depleted transmission fluid additives. The shudder is most noticeable during light acceleration between 25-50 mph as the transmission shifts through 3rd-5th gears.
records.solution: Transmission fluid flush and fill (3x flush procedure). Add transmission shudder fix additive (early intervention). Torque converter replacement. Complete transmission rebuild or replacement if severe.
symptoms: Vibration or shudder during light acceleration
